title: Automated inflight request pruning and customer bridgeplay for hosted API timeout waves
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-28 customer incident we observed sustained hosted API 5xx and timeout spikes for a subset of tenants running long sequence workloads. The spike surfaced as long-tail latency, increased connection backpressure at the edge, and many client-scale refreshes that led to visible customer errors and escalations.

Observed behavior and quick RCA hypothesis:
- Edge gateway queues accumulated many long-lived requests (median seq len > 4k tokens) which created head-of-line blocking for short, low-latency calls.
- The runtime's adaptive batching favored throughput and kept batching windows open; that reduced throughput for short requests when long ones were in flight.
- In several code paths the client's request deadline was not propagated or honored cleanly; canceled clients left inflight contexts that continued using resources until runtime-level timeouts, creating resource pressure and queue saturation.
- Amplification loop: increased client retries (with short deadlines) multiplied active connections -> edge backlog -> more cancellations and delayed cleanup -> elevated 5xx/timeouts.

Temporary mitigations implemented (done):
1) Edge-level inflight-prune toggle: an emergency feature that proactively cancels lowest-priority inflight requests when edge queue depth exceeds threshold (feature gate: edge.inflight_prune). Deployed to prod region us-west-2 behind a kill-switch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234
2) Short-circuit for small requests: prioritize requests with content-length header and sequence-length hint to fastpath queue admission. Deployed as config to edge router (config-id: ER-PRIO-20260301).
3) Client advisory & SDK patch: published advisory to customers and released SDK 1.12.1 that now forwards client deadlines to the API (docs + compatibility notes). Docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Deadline+Propagation+Guide
4) Conversation bridge: created customer-facing bridge playbook and Slack channel for live incident triage; offered emergency credits to affected customers. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Hosted-5xx-Customer-Bridgeplay

Planned long-term fixes (in flight):
A) Proper inbound deadline propagation and context ownership: ensure that when a client cancels the request, the edge and runtime release resources immediately instead of waiting for internal timeouts. This requires change across router -> ingress -> runtime message path (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Deadline-Ownership-2026). Target release: runtime-1.28.
B) Fine-grained batching profiles: implement per-tenant and per-route batching knobs (max-wait, max-batch-bytes) so long-sequence workloads can't keep windows open for short requests. This reduces head-of-line blocking and enables safe tenant-level isolation.
C) Inflight request scoring and graceful eviction: convert the emergency inflight-prune proof-of-concept into a configurable eviction policy with tenant budgets and fairness metrics. The policy will surface metrics so SRE can observe evictions and tune thresholds before customer impact.
D) Telemetry and automated mitigation: extend the alerting rule set to include queue-depth hysteresis and a synthetic short-request probe to detect H-O-L blocking early. Hook alerts to a playbook that can auto-toggle inflight-prune conservatively.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive eviction reduces cold-start throughput for heavy workloads; we budgeted a soft threshold and incremental backoff to avoid repeatedly preempting the same tenant's requests.
- Propagating deadlines adds more RPC bookkeeping in the runtime path; we prioritized correctness and a lightweight context ID approach to minimize CPU overhead.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Canary: rollout inflight-prune to 10% of edge load and synthetic customers with both long and short workloads. Monitor error-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and eviction counts for 72h.
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 7 days with automated rollback on specified SLO regressions.
- Regression tests: unit tests for cancel propagation, e2e harness for small/large request mixes, and chaos test to simulate delayed cleanup.

Next steps (short horizon):
- Complete runtime PR for deadline propagation and land small API for cancel tokens (owner: Ravi) - ETA 2026-03-12.
- Release inflight-prune to 30% after 24h canary with no regression (owner: Mei) - ETA 2026-03-11.
- Prepare customer email + post-incident summary and commit to follow-up teleconf with top 5 impacted customers (owner: Jordan) - ETA 2026-03-13.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Edge inflight-prune hardened and feature-flagged with tenant budgets and observability;
- Runtime honors client deadlines and cancels resources within 200ms of client cancellation;
- p99 short-request latency reduced to baseline within 48h of rollout for impacted tenants;
- Customer communications completed and top customers acknowledge mitigation plan.

2026-03-05 - Design review (internal): Decided to keep eviction policy conservative initially; avoid hard-kills for in-progress billing-critical requests.
2026-03-08 - PR feedback: Security review requested for behavior that cancels inflight requests. Security: low risk but require audit log for evictions. Action: add eviction audit events.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Deployed canary (10%) in us-west-2. Monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/edge/inflight-prune-canary. No customer-visible regressions in first 24h.
2026-03-10 - Jordan Lee: Opened customer bridge with top 3 impacted customers; scheduled follow-up calls for 2026-03-12.
